correctness.rationale: For each nonempty finite \(F\), choosing \(q\notin F-F\) and a sufficiently short interval produces two functions whose finite orbit-coordinate supports are pointwise disjoint, giving the exact identity \(N_F(\alpha u+\beta v)=|\alpha|+|\beta|\). This proves an isometric \(\ell_1^2\) subspace and therefore failure of strict convexity, Gâteaux smoothness and wMLUR. The approximation estimate follows directly from \(\sqrt{A+B}-\sqrt A\le\sqrt B\), the inequality \(\ell_2\le\ell_1\), measure preservation, and \(\sum_k\sqrt{a_k}<\infty\). The full-norm regularity hypotheses match the focal theorem for irrational rotation.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural and exact boundary in a new renorming construction: its wMLUR, strict-convexity and smoothness effects cannot be reproduced at any finite orbit horizon, even though finite horizons approximate the full norm uniformly with an explicit summable tail bound. The exact \(\ell_1^2\) witness explains the failure geometrically rather than merely noting that strict convexity need not survive approximation. This is a motivated structural fact about how the recent Daugavet-compatible rotundity construction uses infinitely many orbit coordinates.
